thread_text:
sam: FYI seeing a repeatable p99 spike during short bursts after the autoscale prober change. p95 looks fine but p99 jumps 2-3x for ~30s windows. :thinking:
deploy-bot: deployed redwood/runtime@v2.9.1 to prod (canary 10% -> 100%)
sam: noticed it on canary then prod when burst hit and scale-up lagged. stack: kernel-selector + microbatcher + KV cache.
mira: any profiler traces? screenshots?
sam: attaching quick capture (snip):
```
p95: 48ms  p99: 318ms  throughput: 120rps
gpu-util: 62%  queue-depth: 14  microbatch-size: 8
trace sample: head wait -> fallback kernel (attn-v2-slow) -> KV miss -> extra 200ms
```
leo: hmm fallback kernel chosen a lot? selector may be flipping to L2-optimized kernel because early samples reported longer seq lengths during the prober's synthetic requests.
avani: prober change earlier today increased synthetic seq len from 128->512 to test perf at long-context. did we leave prober ramp settings the same? :eyes:
sam: yeah prober payloads are longer. prober now sends a 512 context request every Nth probe. i think kernel selector uses a short-window histogram and then chooses variant for the batch. during burst the selector sees spike and picks the slower kernel for many short requests.
mira: that explains slow p99 for short real requests. also saw KV cache eviction rates spike in same window. maybe warmup missed because scale-up created new nodes with empty cache and microbatches drained the old cached prefixes.
jordan: repro steps I ran:
```
# emulate burst
wrk -c200 -t8 --script=burst.lua --duration=60 http://prod-infer
# observe logs
rg "kernel-selector.*choose" /var/log/runtime/*.log | tail -n50
```
log excerpt:
```
[12:01:03] kernel-selector: chose attn-v2-l2 for model@v3 seq_avg=410 window=15
[12:01:04] microbatcher: dispatched batch size=12 (target=8) latency=90ms
[12:01:05] kv-cache: evict rate=0.24/s  miss_rate=0.18  warmup_hits=3
```

leo: microbatcher ramped up to 12 because queue heuristic uses pending-time+util to pick batch size. during the cold-surge the runtime pushed bigger microbatches to keep GPU busy, which increases head-of-line for short requests. that plus wrong kernel variant is a triple-whammy.
avani: autoscaler prober also has a backpressure short-circuit that reduces prober frequency when latency spikes to avoid noise. that meant scale-up lagged longer than usual because probes suppressed.
sam: so root causes: (1) prober payloads biased kernel selector toward slow kernel, (2) microbatcher increased batch size under burst causing extra tail, (3) scale-up inhibited by prober backpressure -> more cold nodes -> kv warmup misses.
mira: can we mitigate quickly? suggestions: revert prober payload to mixed seq lengths, cap microbatch max during burst, and make kernel-selector use per-request seq estimates rather than short-window avg.
leo: pragmatic immediate changes: cap microbatch size to 8 for next 30m in prod for the affected pool, add kernel-selector fallback threshold (only switch if >80% of recent requests), and bump prober ramp to be slower but with diversified seq lengths.
jordan: i can push a hotfix to microbatcher cap and tweak prober payloads. want a quick test in staging.
avani: +1. also add a lightweight KV prewarm hook on scale-up events so new nodes fetch hot prefixes from local LRU store for first 10s. low-risk.
sam: profiling numbers after staging change (short run):
```
baseline (before): p95=48ms p99=318ms
after microbatch cap + mixed prober: p95=50ms p99=78ms  throughput ~115rps
gpu-util: 60% queue-depth: 6  kv-miss=0.02
```

mira: nice improvement, p99 down to acceptable range. can we automate detection? maybe sensor that correlates kernel-variant-shift + kv-evict spike -> automatic rollback of prober.
leo: yes we can add a short-circuit: if p99 > 200ms and kernel_variant_switch_rate > 30% within 15s, pause prober and reduce microbatch target.
avani: note: need to avoid thrashing on noisy signals. we'll add hysteresis and require 3 consecutive windows.
jordan: I'll submit the PR for microbatch cap + prober payload revert + KV prewarm hook. marking as hotfix.
ci-bot: CI passed for pr/4582 (microbatch cap) -> merged to main.
sam: rolling the cap to prod now, will monitor. thanks all. :thumbsup:
mira: follow-up items for next week sprint: kernel-selector long-tail analysis, prober diversification, KV prewarm telemetry + dashboard. I'll create tickets.
sam: logging task ids in thread: T-1123 (kernel selector analysis), T-1124 (prober diversification), T-1125 (kv prewarm + metric).
avani: good, add simulation tests to prober repo so we don't regress again.
leo: also add microbatching unit that simulates short-request-heavy bursts to CI.
sam: closing loop once stable for 2h. will update thread. :eyes:
